title: Empirical throughput sweeps and customer acceptance protocol for Dedicated pools
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Why: Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect predictable throughput under realistic application traffic. Current synthetic benchmarks show peak tokens/sec but do not capture request shape variance, autoscaler hysteresis, or fallback behavior across model variants. This ticket defines an empirical sweep methodology, implements a repeatable load harness that replays realistic profiles, and produces a customer-facing acceptance protocol and artifacts for signoff.
deliverables: A documented sweep methodology that covers steady-state, ramp, burst, and tail-latency scenarios
A containerized load harness (k8s Job + orchestrator) capable of running parameterized sweeps across pool sizes and model variants
A standard customer acceptance checklist and pass/fail JSON report schema
Automated dashboards and an artifact bundle (CSV + traces) uploaded to the release folder
Runbook snippets for Solutions/SE to run on customer Dedicated pools
harness_architecture: Controller: orchestrates sweeps, coordinates traffic generators, and uploads artifacts to S3 (s3://redwood-dedicated-sweeps/)
Traffic generators: Go-based microservice that replays recorded profiles with configurable fanout, qps, and token distribution
Telemetry collector: samples Prometheus + Jaeger traces, aggregates token counts and latency histograms every 10s
Validator: post-run analysis script that computes P50/P95/P99 latencies, tokens/sec, error rates, autoscaler events, and KV cache hit ratios
Packaging: Docker image + Helm chart to install the harness into a test project or customer VPC
traffic_profiles: Synth-steady: constant QPS set to 60% of published pool capacity; uniform length 64 tokens
Synth-burst: baseline at 10% capacity with 30s bursts to 120% to exercise autoscaler and fallback
Application-replay: recorded request traces from three customers (chat, search, summarization) with diode-shaped interarrival times
Tail-latency stress: 1% of requests stamped as high-cost (length 512 + complex system prompt) to measure cache eviction impact
Mix-and-match: randomized mix of model variants and quantization profiles to validate routing and graceful degradation
metrics: tokens_per_second: measured aggregate successful tokens emitted per second during sweep windows
requests_per_second: QPS at the API surface (requests/s)
p50_p95_p99_latency_ms: end-to-end API latencies including scheduling and queuing
error_rate: percent of requests with 5xx or model-fallback errors
autoscaler_events: timestamps and reasons for scale-up/scale-down events
kv_cache_hit_ratio: fraction of prefix cache hits per request
cost_estimate_usd_per_hour: projected infra cost for scenario using current instance pricing
test_plan: Step 1 - Prepare: provision a test Dedicated pool matching customer commit (GPUs, node count, model pinning). Capture current autoscaler config.
Step 2 - Baseline: run Synth-steady at 30% capacity for 10 minutes to capture idle behavior and warm kernel caches.
Step 3 - Sweep: iterate QPS from 30% -> 120% in 10% increments with 5-minute dwell, record metrics and autoscaler events.
Step 4 - Burst testing: schedule 5x short bursts (30s) to 120-150% capacity, measure queuing and fallback incidence.
Step 5 - Replay: run Application-replay profile for 30 minutes, collect traces, and compute regressions vs baseline.
Step 6 - Acceptance report: run Validator to produce JSON report; compare to acceptance criteria and upload bundle to release folder.
Step 7 - Customer signoff: hand off artifact bundle and run summary to SE for customer-facing walkthrough and signoff checklist completion.
acceptance_criteria: Throughput: sustained tokens_per_second >= 95% of contracted throughput for three consecutive 5-minute windows during the Sweep phase.
Tail latency: P99 latency must be <= the contractual P99 + 30% buffer under steady load (Synth-steady).
Error rate: end-to-end error_rate <= 0.5% across all runs; any model-fallback counts must be logged with root cause.
Autoscaler behavior: scale-ups must occur within configured SLO (default 60s) for ramps; unnecessary scale-churn (scale up/down within 2 minutes) triggers investigation.
KV cache: primary workloads must show cache hit_ratio >= 70% after warm-up for chat-style workloads; if lower, capture prefix distribution and file bug.
Reproducibility: rerunning the same sweep within the same pool config yields metric variance within 7% for tokens_per_second and 15% for P99 latency.
Customer-ready report: JSON pass/fail and human-readable summary uploaded and reviewed by PM and SE.
runbook_snippets: helm install dedicated-sweep ./charts/dedicated-sweep --namespace sweep-runner --set poolName=<POOL> --set image.tag=v2026-03

# start a parameterized sweep (example)
kubectl exec -n sweep-runner deploy/controller -- /controller run --profile synth-burst --qps-start 0.3 --qps-end 1.2 --dwell 300

# collect artifact bundle after run
kubectl cp sweep-runner/controller:/artifacts/2026-03-10-bundle.tar.gz ./2026-03-10-bundle.tar.gz

# validate locally
python validator.py --input artifacts/2026-03-10.json --thresholds config/acceptance-thresholds.yaml
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Autoscaler config differences between test and customer pool can invalidate results. Mitigation: include a step to export and attach the actual customer autoscaler YAML and use it in test cluster when possible.
Risk: Noise from co-located workloads on shared infra. Mitigation: tag test pools as isolation=true or schedule tests in maintenance windows and record cluster noise metrics.
Risk: Incomplete replay fidelity (missing model variants or prompt complexity). Mitigation: add 'complexity stamps' to recorded traces and annotate any missing behaviors in the report.
Risk: Long sweep time increases cost. Mitigation: provide a fast-check mode (reduced dwell times) and a full-cert mode for customer signoff.
